questions.q: What are the four sensitivity tiers used in this lesson's classification scheme?
options: Green, Yellow, Orange, Red
Low, Medium, High, Critical
Open, Closed, Locked, Encrypted
Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted
questions.explain: The lesson's classification table defines exactly these four tiers, each with a meaning and an LTV Global example.

questions.q: Why does Payments.CardToken land in the Restricted tier even though it's a token, not a raw card number?
options: All tokens are automatically classified as Public
Tokens are never considered sensitive under any scheme
Classification follows the consequence of exposure (PCI scope, mandatory breach disclosure), not just the literal content of the field
Restricted only applies to data stored in Comet
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states that the impact of mishandling the token — PCI exposure and mandatory disclosure — drives its tier, not whether the raw digits are present.

questions.q: What tier was assigned to Customers.Email, and why?
options: Restricted — it requires a formal breach response like the card token
Public — anyone can see any customer's email
Confidential — it is personal data under UK/California privacy law and was the element behind the Lesson 1 DSAR
It was not classified at all
questions.explain: Email is flagged Confidential: limited to people who need it for their job, directly tied to the privacy-law exposure from the Lesson 1 incident.

questions.q: What overlooked element did the classification pass surface, and where does it come from?
options: Customers.DateOfBirth, captured by Comet during warranty registration for age-restricted gear
A brand-new system no one had heard of
An element that turned out not to exist
Products.SKU, which had already been classified
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out DateOfBirth as a newly surfaced Confidential-tier element worth reconsidering as a CDE candidate.

questions.q: Why were Products.SKU and Orders.OrderTotal classified as Internal rather than Confidential or Restricted?
options: They are published on the public Comet storefront
They contain no data of any kind
Internal is reserved only for payment data
They are commercially sensitive but not personal data about an identifiable individual
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes Internal (commercially sensitive, non-personal) from Confidential/Restricted (personal or regulated data), placing SKU and OrderTotal in the former.
